sources.title: Gemini CLI hooks
sources.locator: What are hooks; Hook events; Security and risks
passages: Hooks run synchronously as part of the agent loop
sources.summary: Lifecycle command hooks run synchronously; project hook name/command changes trigger new untrusted-hook warning. SessionStart covers startup, resume and clear. BeforeAgent runs after user prompt.

sources.title: Gemini CLI hooks reference
sources.locator: Global hook mechanics; Base input schema; BeforeAgent; SessionStart (web extraction lines 267-277, 308-325, 422-434, 520-539)
passages: Text that is appended to the prompt for this turn only.
sources.summary: stdin JSON fields include session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name and timestamp. stdout must be JSON only, stderr is log/feedback; code 0 parses JSON, code 2 blocks, other failures warn and continue. BeforeAgent additionalContext adds per-turn context; SessionStart context enters first history turn in interactive mode or prefixes noninteractive prompt. Startup ignores decision/continue. timeout milliseconds default 60000. Only command hook execution engine is documented.

sources.title: Gemini CLI configuration
passages: Displays the version of the CLI.
sources.summary: User settings are ~/.gemini/settings.json; project settings .gemini/settings.json override user; system settings override all, with GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH override. --resume accepts latest/index/full UUID; --prompt is noninteractive, --prompt-interactive gives initial interactive input. --version exists.

sources.title: OpenCode Plugins
sources.locator: From local files; Basic structure; Shell Events; Inject environment variables; Compaction hooks (lines 108-157, 216-244, 310-337, 409-433, 525-618)
passages: Files in these directories are automatically loaded at startup.
Inject environment variables into all shell execution (AI tools and user terminals)
sources.summary: JavaScript/TypeScript modules auto-load from .opencode/plugins and ~/.config/opencode/plugins. Factory receives project, client, shell API, directory, worktree and returns hooks object. All sources load in sequence; duplicate npm same-name/version dedupes but local plus npm are separate. session.created/idle/status and other events documented. shell.env permits mutable per-shell environment. experimental.session.compacting supports context or replacing prompt; replacement ignores context array.

sources.title: OpenCode plugin Hooks types (development branch)
passages: input: { cwd: string; sessionID?: string; callID?: string }
sources.summary: shell.env has optional sessionID/callID: caller attribution cannot assume every shell event belongs to a session. chat.message, tool.execute.before/after have sessionID. experimental.chat.system.transform has optional sessionID and mutable system string array. Experimental compaction hook is session-specific. dispose callback exists. Source on mutable dev branch is authoritative code but not pinned release evidence.

sources.title: OpenCode CLI
sources.locator: tui flags; attach; run flags; environment variables (lines 146-158, 217-255, 575-595, 955-969)
sources.summary: --session/-s, --continue/-c and --fork supported. run provides noninteractive command plus --attach server mode, --dir and --format json. TUI can attach to existing backend. OPENCODE_CONFIG, OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR and OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT give file/directory/inline config; --version prints version. An adapter cannot infer backend caller identity from the TUI terminal process when using attach.

sources.title: Pi Extensions (current canonical docs)
sources.locator: Create and load; Respect runtime lifecycle; Events and concurrency (lines 10-57, 79-103)
sources.summary: Extensions run inside Pi with same OS permissions. Default factory receives ExtensionAPI; jiti loads local TS without compilation; global/project extension discovery and explicit --extension supported. Async factory is awaited, but must not start long-lived resources because invocations may only load extensions; resources should start at session_start and close at idempotent session_shutdown. agent_end may precede recovery/retries/queued work; agent_settled marks true final boundary. before_agent_start permits prompt mutation and persistent custom message; context transforms differ in ownership.

sources.title: Pi extension event types (current main)
sources.locator: SessionStartEvent lines 677-683; BeforeAgentStartEvent lines 840-850; BeforeAgentStartEventResult lines 1352-1356
sources.summary: SessionStartEvent consolidates startup/reload/new/resume/fork with previousSessionFile for latter transitions. before_agent_start exposes prompt and mutable systemPromptOptions plus optional complete systemPrompt replacement. Custom context message return has content/customType/display/details. These are in-process typed callbacks, not command-hook stdin/out.

sources.title: Pi Configuration
passages: Project configuration lives in `.pi` under the working directory
sources.summary: Default user agent directory ~/.pi/agent can be overridden by PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR or SDK agentDir. Project config loads only after trust granted; sessionDir read before trust is exception.

sources.title: Pi Command Line
passages: Shows the Pi version, then exits.
Opens by file path, exact ID, or partial ID.
sources.summary: --session accepts path/exact/partial ID and may offer cross-project fork; --session-id exact project ID can create if absent. --resume is picker, --continue latest project. --fork explicit new session. --session-dir overrides storage env/config, --no-session ephemeral. --extension repeatable adds explicit runtime bridge; --no-extensions still allows explicit -e. --append-system-prompt appends; --approve trusts project config for one process and --no-approve ignores it. RPC/JSON modes reserve stdout; terminal redirection affects default mode. -v/--version exists.

sources.title: Pi Session Format
passages: First line of the file. Metadata only, not part of the tree
sources.summary: Session JSONL header id/cwd and optional parentSession record explicit fork/clone ancestry. Tree entries have parentId referring to entries, not parent agents. Treat ancestry differently from harness-created child agent attribution.

implications.text: Cohesive adapter should own bridge assets and invocation shape. Normalize lifecycle/context intents in core but leave JS/TS callbacks, stdin/out codecs, event-to-intent mapping, stdout reservation and timeout units adapter-local. A mandatory command-hook implementation excludes OpenCode/Pi without scattered exceptions.

Lifecycle capability cannot be a boolean or single universal start/stop pair: startup may be advisory only; session start includes clear/reload/fork and stop may mean turn ended or finally settled. Adapter observations need explicit semantic reason and context lifetime, and unsupported guarantees must remain unsupported.

Setup plan should distinguish owned executable/bridge assets from edits to shared settings, discovery locations, launch-only injection and native trust/approval effects. Native approval must remain user-visible; installation must not add --approve or otherwise manufacture admission success.

Session/caller/child observations require distinct optional provenance. Optional OpenCode session IDs and detached backend/TUI topology prevent assuming terminal environment belongs to every agent action. Pi parentSession and tree parentId prove branching relationships only, not child-agent identity.

Launch spec should be typed executable+argv+env with explicit fresh/resume/fork mode and resume token format; avoid shared --resume convention. Version readout needs separate installed binary observation from documented recipe/code revision and native probe evidence.

gaps_and_counterevidence: No binary was installed/launched; all findings are documentation/code evidence, never native PASS.
No release versions/commit hashes were pinned. Mutable docs/main/dev cannot establish minimum supported version.

Pi older indexed fork docs use @mariozechner packages and distinct session_switch/session_fork; direct current badlogic docs link to earendil-works/pi and current session_start reasons differ. Recipes must target observed installed version instead of search snippets.

OpenCode simultaneously publishes legacy docs and /v2/docs using plugins plural/new service architecture; this audit uses /docs plus anomalyco/opencode dev types. Selecting v1 versus v2 requires installed-version evidence before any support claim.

Native subagent child markers and exact environment inheritance were not established for these three harnesses. shell.env is a mutation mechanism, not evidence of a correct herdr child marker implementation.
No supported universal hook guarantees receipt durability, seat continuity or native consent. Those remain herdr daemon/core policy responsibilities.
Pi explicit extension launch may avoid persistent config edits, but launch-only injection does not establish coverage of independently started Pi sessions.
Gemini additionalContext differs between SessionStart and BeforeAgent; forcing one renderer/lifetime would silently change behavior.
retrieval_stop: Three independent harnesses expose the intended material variations (command protocol versus in-process bridge; advisory versus actionable lifecycle; per-turn versus persistent context; discovery and trust; detached backend and optional session identity; branching versus child). Further harness breadth is unnecessary for design preview. Remaining native/version/child gaps are explicit follow-up work rather than assumptions.
